chunks: ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from Isḥāq ibn Muḥammad, from Shāhawayh ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Jallāb, who said:

Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام wrote to me in a letter: “You wanted to ask about the successor after Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, and you were anxious about that, so do not grieve; for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, does not cause a people to go astray after He has guided them until He makes clear to them what they should guard against.”
“And your master after me is Abū Muḥammad, my son, and with him is what you need. Allah advances what He wills and delays what He wills.”
“Whatever āyah We abrogate or cause to be forgotten, We bring one better than it or one like it.”
“I have written that in which there is clarification and sufficiency for one who possesses an alert intellect.”

key_terms.آيَةٍ: a sign or verse, here in the cited Qur'anic expression
key_terms.أَبُو مُحَمَّدٍ: Abū Muḥammad عليه السلام, identified here as the succeeding Imam
key_terms.الْخَلَفِ: the successor who comes after a preceding Imam
key_terms.لَا يُضِلُّ: does not leave astray or cause to stray after guidance has been given
key_terms.يُؤَخِّرُ: He delays or puts back by divine will
key_terms.يُقَدِّمُ: He brings forward, advances, or gives precedence by divine will

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith indicate the Imamate of Abū Muḥammad عليه السلام after Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith records a written designation by Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام of Abū Muḥammad عليه السلام as the successor after Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, reassuring the questioner that Allah does not leave the community misguided after guidance without clarification. It also invokes a Qur'anic principle about divine replacement and ordering, emphasizing that religious authority and succession unfold by Allah’s will and clear proof.
